script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for April 3. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You can describe a sunset to someone who wasn't there.  You can warn a stranger about danger.  You can pass on knowledge you'll never use yourself.

Human language has a remarkable property: from a limited set of sounds and rules, we can generate an infinite number of sentences. You can say things never said before. Every sentence in this lesson could be completely novel. Children acquire language without formal instruction—exposed to speech, they naturally develop grammar.  This suggests language isn't just learned; it's built into the human brain.

Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Language isn't just communication—it's the technology that lets human knowledge accumulate across generations.  Every word you speak connects you to a chain of minds stretching back to our species' beginnings.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Language Appreciation - Notice the Miracle.

Here's your activity: Today, notice one thing you can only do because of language: explain an abstract idea, discuss the past, plan for tomorrow, or imagine something fictional. Language makes these possible. Appreciate the superpower you use constantly. This helps you develop appreciation for language's unique power.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why humans have language can be applied to language appreciation - notice the miracle. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
